clue.text: A Lord's match? He's going

definitions.meaning: a lord's equal in rank is another noble of the same standing, a member of the House of Lords
a jokey noun for someone who is 'going' in the toilet sense, i.e. one who urinates

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a toilet joke: someone who pees, written as a noun. 'Going' is a coy word for relieving oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobleman's equal is a fellow noble, and the word also splits into a slangy noun for someone urinating.

clue.text: Places to leave motor boats weighed down by fish

indicators.note: in a down clue the boats sit below the fish, pressing it from beneath

parts.note: the carp is a freshwater fish
an ark is a boat, as in Noah's

explanation.surface: Motor boats are being sunk under a load of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motor boats' reads as one thing; 'motor' belongs to the definition (somewhere to leave a car) and 'boats' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: These are lots where drivers leave their vehicles standing; motor is a British word for car.

clue.text: City End's toilets

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, the city
'end' as a verb, third person: something that ends expires

explanation.surface: Talk of the lavatories at one end of a football ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'End's' is read as the verb form 'ends', meaning expires.
explanation.definitionFit: The women's public conveniences are signposted with this word in Britain.

clue.text: Killer, one shut up in prison

indicators.note: the numeral is locked inside the word for jail

parts.note: the can is slang for jail
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A murderer is one of those locked up in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's first murderer, who slew his brother Abel.

clue.text: Against Spain, an example of Moore's passing

indicators.note: placed against, i.e. right beside, the next piece

parts.note: Demi Moore, the actress, gives her first name with the possessive S
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: Moore's death described against a Spanish backdrop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moore's' could be Roger, Bobby or Dudley; it is Demi Moore, possessive giving the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing is a gentle word for death, and this noun means the same end of life.

clue.text: This, for one, is not even cultured

indicators.note: keep only the odd-numbered letters of the word, dropping the even ones

explanation.surface: A claim that something is not even refined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This, for one' points at the very thing the solver is reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The sentence the solver is reading is an example of a crossword hint, self-referentially.

clue.text: Win at home? No, I don't believe it!

parts.note: to win something is to get it
not at home, i.e. playing on the opponent's ground

explanation.surface: Disbelief at a home win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' turns 'at home' into its opposite, the sporting term for a fixture on the other side's ground.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of incredulity, like 'you're joking!' or 'pull the other one!'

clue.text: Cooked meal all over plate

indicators.note: food that is cooked is altered, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A cooked meal served entirely over a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plate' looks like crockery; it means a thin layer, as in anatomy or botany.
explanation.definitionFit: A technical term for a thin layer, scale or membrane, such as the gills of a mushroom.

clue.text: Journey time not quite ready

indicators.note: lose the final letter, so the word is not complete

parts.note: fruit that is ready to eat is ripe

explanation.surface: Time for a journey is not quite ready.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing or excursion; a short journey.

clue.text: Popular outlet — setter's showing creativity

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
a vent is an outlet for air or steam
the setter speaks as I, so setter's = I have, contracted

explanation.surface: A setter shows creativity through a popular outlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter's' is read as 'setter has', i.e. I've.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for someone original and imaginative, good at devising new things.

clue.text: Gassy state? Deep-fried Indian breads contain zero gas

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a US state

indicators.note: the breads hold the zero inside them

parts.note: puris are small puffed fried breads from India
O looks like zero
H is the chemical symbol of hydrogen, a gas

explanation.surface: A culinary riddle: fried breads stuffed with nothing but air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gassy state?' looks like the definition, but 'state' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for something like vapour, misty or airy; it can also mean flighty.

clue.text: SE Asian native, one displaying bloomers after stripping off

indicators.note: the outer layer of letters is removed, both ends

parts.note: a flower seller shows off blooms; bloomers are flowers here, not underwear

explanation.surface: Someone showing off their underwear after undressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' suggests knickers; here it means plants that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow-moving nocturnal primate of South and Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Undone by game against Home Counties

parts.note: loo is an old card game
the counties around London lie in the South East of England, SE

explanation.surface: A defeat in a match against the Home Counties.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties surround London, in the South East.
explanation.definitionFit: Untied or unfastened, as a knot or shoelace can be.

clue.text: Clap team off — one in top of table setting

definitions.text: one in top of table setting

indicators.note: something gone off has spoiled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Stop applauding the team at the top of the league table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top of table' suggests a league leader; it is the literal top of a dining table.
explanation.definitionFit: A small mat set at each diner's place on a laid table.

clue.text: Ratings for muscles

definitions.meaning: able seamen, AB, are naval ratings; plural

explanation.definitionFit: Sailors of lowest rank and the stomach muscles share this short plural form.

clue.text: Marble top taken from kitchen

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a galley is a ship's kitchen

explanation.surface: A marble worktop removed from a kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marble top' reads as a worktop, but 'Marble' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A choice glass or stone playing marble, used as a shooter.

clue.text: On reflection, crossword has them

indicators.note: seen as in a mirror, the letters come out backwards
the word holds the letters inside it

explanation.surface: Thinking about it, a crossword grid contains these.
explanation.walkthrough: The four letters sit backwards in the middle of 'crossword'.
explanation.definitionFit: Horizontal lines of squares, which every crossword grid contains.

clue.text: Devices worn on boots in 22A

definitions.meaning: pointed devices on a rider's heels to urge a horse on
the nickname of the north London football club based there

explanation.definitionFit: A rider's heel prods, and the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur football club.

clue.text: Day of the week for a rising setter

definitions.meaning: short form for the first day of the week
the star that rises in the east and sets in the west

explanation.walkthrough: A 'setter' is normally the compiler; here it is something that sets in the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation for the day of rest, and the star that both rises and sets daily.

clue.text: Location of shopping arcade? Likely in the centre

indicators.note: the letters sit in the middle of these words

explanation.surface: Asking where the shopping arcade is: probably in the town centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a shop, so a place where shopping happens.

clue.text: Got less done, with daughter replacing son

indicators.note: one letter stands where the other stood

parts.note: to be done is to be cheated or conned

explanation.surface: Less work got done once the daughter took over from the son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got less done' reads as one phrase; the definition is 'Got less' and 'done' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink or diminish gradually, past tense: became smaller.

clue.text: Small bird, say, born in small Asian capital

indicators.note: spoken, the bird's name drops its silent first letter

parts.note: the wren is a tiny songbird

indicators.note: the born letter goes inside the word for small

parts.note: mini means small

explanation.surface: A small bird born in a small Asian capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a city; it is money, the currency of China.
explanation.definitionFit: The official currency of China; capital means money, and the yuan is its unit.

clue.text: What one might pass in Test before smooth run-out

indicators.note: the test comes in front of the next piece

parts.note: the MOT is the annual UK roadworthiness test for vehicles

indicators.note: R, the cricket abbreviation for run, is taken out

parts.note: to iron is to smooth

explanation.surface: A cricket Test, before a smooth run-out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket; the MOT is the UK annual car test.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal proposal put to a meeting, which members may pass by vote.

clue.text: Friendship or sex, in a setter's case

indicators.note: the sex word goes inside the other letters
the outer letters form a case around it

parts.note: the setter speaks as me, so setter's is my
it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: Wondering whether it was friendship or sex, in the setter's own case.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun for friendly relations, harmony and goodwill between people.

clue.text: Nearly lost a match, only header worked

indicators.note: letters worked over are reshaped into a new order
just the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: A football match nearly lost, only a header winning it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'header' looks like football; it signals the first letter of 'match'.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning very nearly, all but.

clue.text: The man running after a small child somewhere in London

indicators.note: the reordered piece comes after the child

parts.note: a tot is a toddler

indicators.note: the letters run about freely, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: A man running to catch a toddler.
explanation.definitionFit: A district of north London, home of the football club.

clue.text: Conversely, side fall heavily

indicators.note: read as con-verse-ly, in conversation, so the word is spoken

parts.note: a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: On the other hand, a side may fall heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conversely' is a pun: 'in conversation', spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain that comes down in torrents pours or buckets down.

clue.text: Fine chap, if somewhat hysterical

indicators.note: only a part of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A fine fellow, if a little hysterical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine chap' simply means a man's name; 'Eric, or Little by Little' is a moralising Victorian school story.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name, so any man bearing it is a chap.

clue.text: Awful finisher, reportedly?

indicators.note: as it is said, the word sounds alike

parts.note: a cloth dyer gives textiles their finish, colouring them

explanation.surface: An awful player who fails to score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finisher' suggests a striker; a dyer finishes cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for something dreadful or terrible.

clue.text: Career in a rock group

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to career is to hurtle or dash
a Canadian progressive rock band of that name

explanation.definitionFit: To hurtle headlong, and the name of a famous Canadian rock trio.

clue.text: Spanish guitarist goes touring the Italian way

indicators.note: going around, so the letters are turned about

parts.note: via is Italian for road or way

explanation.surface: A Spanish guitarist goes on tour the Italian way.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrés, the great Spanish classical guitarist of the 20th century.

clue.text: Badmouth a team here, with very loose talk?

indicators.note: very loosely pronounced, the phrase sounds like the word

parts.note: Spurs, the team from 22A, with 'a' before it

explanation.surface: Trash-talking a team with careless chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: The team 'here' is Spurs (17A), the London club; the sound match is admitted loose.
explanation.definitionFit: To slander or cast aspersions on someone, criticise them unfairly.
